Use this numbered guide with the Home screen image:

1. Quick Start: reconnects to the last saved Bluetooth device, or sends you to scan for a new device.

2. RC Control Screen: opens the landscape controller used to drive the RC project.

3. RC Settings: opens the controller settings for UI style, joystick behavior, switch defaults, and knob defaults.

4. Select UI: reserved for choosing the controller style; for now, change the style from RC Settings.

5. Bluetooth: opens the device list to scan, connect, and check the current connection status.

6. Codes and Documents: opens PDF guides and lets you share or save the ESP32_BT_Controller-main.zip code file.

7. Tutorial: opens this step-by-step app guide.

8. Help: top-right shortcut for quick help when the app guide is connected to it.

This video shows how to prepare the ESP32 in Arduino IDE:

- Open ESP32_BT_Controller.ino in Arduino IDE (download the ZIP from the app in step 2 if you do not have the sketch yet).

- Select the correct ESP32 board under Tools > Board.

- Select the serial port connected to your ESP32 under Tools > Port.

- Upload the sketch to the ESP32.

- Open Tools > Serial Monitor and set the baud rate to 115200.

- Press the ESP32 RESET button.

- Confirm the monitor prints: ESP32 Bluetooth Receiver Ready.

- When you see that message, the ESP32 is waiting for a Bluetooth connection from the app (step 4).

This video shows how to get the project files from the app:

- Open Codes and Documents on the Home screen and tap the ESP32 BT Controller ZIP item.

- Choose Share or send to email or messaging, or Save to Downloads to keep a copy on the phone.

- Open the ZIP where you saved it or from the app you shared to.

- Extract the archive if needed and locate ESP32_BT_Controller.ino.

- Transfer the folder to your computer if you uploaded from the phone, then continue with step 3 in Arduino IDE.
Connect to the ESP32 with Bluetooth

This GIF shows how to connect the app to the ESP32-BT device:

- From the Home screen, tap the Bluetooth button.

- On the Bluetooth screen, tap the refresh icon in the top app bar to start scanning.

- When ESP32-BT appears, tap the X icon to stop scanning.

- Check the Scanned Devices list and find ESP32-BT.

- If this is the first connection, tap ESP32-BT from Scanned Devices to pair and connect.

- If the ESP32 was already paired before, tap ESP32-BT from Paired Devices to connect faster.

- After the connection succeeds, the app returns to the Home screen.

- Confirm that the Bluetooth button now shows the Connected status.

This GIF shows how to review and apply the controller settings:

- From the Home screen, tap the settings button beside RC Control Screen.

- On RC Controller Settings, review RC Screen Style and choose the controller interface you want to use.

- Review Joystick Settings and choose the behavior for the left and right sticks.

- Review Initial Switch Positions and set the starting state for switches S1 to S6.

- Review Initial Knob Values and set the starting value for the left and right knobs.

- Return to the Home screen after the configuration is saved.

- Tap RC Control Screen to open the controller.

- Confirm that the selected UI style, joystick behavior, switch states, and knob values are applied correctly on the RC screen.

- Replace the placeholder GIF with your own recording of the RC Control screen when it is ready.

- Connect the phone to the ESP32 over Bluetooth before recording so control and telemetry match the firmware.

- The RC screen opens in landscape and sends control packets while it stays open.

- In the Arduino IDE, open Serial Monitor at 115200 baud to follow firmware messages (for example client connected or waiting states).

- Optional: in `debug_config.h`, set `DEBUG_ENABLED` to 1 to print high-level connection and receive diagnostics while you explore the layout.

- Replace the placeholder GIF with a clip that moves only the left joystick.

- In `debug_config.h`, enable `DEBUG_ENABLED` and set `DBG_STICKS` to 1, then reflash the ESP32.

- Open Serial Monitor at 115200 baud and connect the app to the ESP32.

- Move the left stick; you should see lines such as `L Stick X:` and `L Stick Y:` updating roughly in the 0 to 1023 range with center near 512.

- If numbers stay flat while the stick moves, verify Bluetooth connection and that stick debug is enabled.

- Replace the placeholder GIF with a clip that moves only the right joystick.

- Keep `DEBUG_ENABLED` and `DBG_STICKS` enabled as in the left stick step.

- Open Serial Monitor at 115200 baud with the app connected.

- Move the right stick; expect `R Stick X:` and `R Stick Y:` style lines to change with the same typical range as the left stick.

- Center both sticks when finished so the robot returns to a neutral command.

- Replace the placeholder GIF with a clip that rotates only the left knob.

- In `debug_config.h`, enable `DEBUG_ENABLED` and set `DBG_KNOBS` to 1, then reflash.

- Open Serial Monitor at 115200 baud and connect the app.

- Turn the left knob; you should see `Left Knob:` values update as the knob moves.

- These values map to the 0 to 1023 style range used for auxiliary parameters in the firmware.

- Replace the placeholder GIF with a clip that rotates only the right knob.

- Keep `DBG_KNOBS` enabled with `DEBUG_ENABLED` set to 1.

- Use Serial Monitor at 115200 baud while the app is connected.

- Adjust the right knob and confirm `Right Knob:` lines track the motion.

- Return knobs to a safe default before driving hardware.
Left switches S1 to S3 (placeholder GIF)

- Replace the placeholder GIF with a clip that toggles only the three switches on the left column.

- Enable `DEBUG_ENABLED` and `DBG_SWITCHES` in `debug_config.h`, then reflash.

- Open Serial Monitor at 115200 baud with the app connected.

- Flip S1, S2, and S3; expect a `Switch Byte:` line plus per-switch lines such as `S1 = ON` for the bits that changed.

- If the byte never changes, confirm Bluetooth data is arriving and that switch debug is enabled.
Right switches S4 to S6 (placeholder GIF)

- Replace the placeholder GIF with a clip that toggles only the three switches on the right column.

- Keep `DBG_SWITCHES` enabled as in the left switch step.

- Watch Serial Monitor at 115200 baud while toggling S4, S5, and S6.

- The same `Switch Byte:` format encodes all six switches, so right-side toggles update the combined pattern together with any left switches.

- Leave switches in a safe configuration before running motors or relays.

- Replace the placeholder GIF with a clip that presses each center-area action button (top and bottom on left and right).

- Enable `DEBUG_ENABLED` and `DBG_EVENTS` in `debug_config.h`, then reflash.

- Open Serial Monitor at 115200 baud and connect the app.

- Tap each button; you should see an event packet dump such as `--- EVENT PACKET (PRESS) ---` with an event id and checksum.

- If no event lines appear, verify Bluetooth connectivity and that event debug is enabled.
